title: Target Controlled Dialysis of Antimicrobials - a non-randomized prospective interventional pilot study
summary: This research project proposes a method for stabilizing the concentration of important anti-infective substances in the blood of intensive care patients, particularly those undergoing renal replacement therapy. The idea is to utilize the physical principles of dialysis to prevent the breakdown of these substances during treatment. To achieve this, the dialysis solution is enriched with a concentration of the anti-infective agent matching the desired level in the blood. Through the exchange of substances across the dialysis membrane, it ensures that the concentration in the blood does not fall below this target level. Previous laboratory experiments have validated this concept. The aim of this pilot study is to verify these findings in intensive care patients.

interventions.name: Addition of an anti-infective agent, which the patient already receives irrespective of the study, in a specific target concentration in the dialysis solution bags

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Study-independent dialysis therapy is being performed.
Study-independent therapy using one of the medications provided for in the study protocol (Meropenem, Piperacillin/Tazobactam, Ceftazidime, Vancomycin, Flucloxacillin).
Desired target concentration of routine therapy is within the range specified in the study protocol.
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 18 years.
Patient and/or legal representative refuse to participate.
Suspected or confirmed overdose with any of the anti-infective medications specified in the study protocol, and use of dialysis with the intention of 'detoxification'
